data.name: Present tense: verbs end in -r
data.explain: Swedish verbs in the present tense usually end in -r: talar, bor, läser, går. The form is the same for every person: jag bor, du bor, hon bor, vi bor.
data.howToSpot: Look for the verb ending in -r near the start of each sentence.

data.name: Two kinds of nouns: en and ett
data.explain: Every Swedish noun is either an en-word or an ett-word, and "a/an" is en or ett to match. Most nouns are en-words, so learn each new noun together with its en or ett.
data.howToSpot: Look for en or ett right before a noun.

data.name: "The" goes on the end: bilen, huset
data.explain: Swedish puts "the" at the end of the noun. En-words add -en or -n (bilen, flickan) and ett-words add -et or -t (huset, äpplet).
data.howToSpot: Look for nouns ending in -en, -n, -et or -t that mean "the …".

data.explain: Swedish nouns form the plural with an ending: -or (flickor), -ar (bilar), -er (katter), -n (äpplen) or no ending at all (barn, hus). Learn the plural together with the word.
data.howToSpot: Look for nouns that mean more than one, often after a number or många.

data.name: Verb second: I dag regnar det
data.explain: In a Swedish statement the verb is always the second part. So when a sentence starts with a time or a place, the subject moves after the verb: I dag regnar det, not "I dag det regnar".
data.howToSpot: Look for sentences that start with a time or place; the verb comes before the subject.

data.name: Questions: the verb comes first
data.explain: In a yes/no question the verb comes first: Bor du här? In a question with a question word (vad, var, när, hur, vem) the verb comes right after that word: Var bor du?
data.howToSpot: Look for a sentence ending in ?, and the verb at the start or right after the question word.

data.name: Not: inte comes after the verb
data.explain: To say "not", put inte after the verb: Jag dricker inte kaffe. Swedish needs no helper like English "do". If the subject comes after the verb, inte comes after the subject: I dag arbetar jag inte.
data.howToSpot: Look for inte and the verb just before it.

data.name: My and your: min, mitt, mina
data.explain: Words like "my" change to match the noun: min with en-words (min bil), mitt with ett-words (mitt hus) and mina in the plural (mina barn). Din, ditt, dina ("your") and vår, vårt, våra ("our") work the same way.
data.howToSpot: Look for min, mitt, mina, din, ditt, dina, vår, vårt or våra before a noun.

data.name: Past tense: -ade, -de, -te and strong verbs
data.explain: The past tense is the same for every person. Regular verbs end in -ade, -de or -te (pratade, stängde, köpte); strong verbs change their vowel instead (gick, åt, drack, var).
data.howToSpot: Look for verbs ending in -ade, -de or -te, or short forms like var, gick, åt, kom.

data.name: Perfect tense: har + supine (har ätit)
data.explain: The perfect tense is har plus the supine form of the verb: jag har ätit, vi har bott. As in English, it is for things that happened at no stated time or are still going on. With a past time like i går, use the past tense.
data.howToSpot: Look for har followed by a verb ending in -at, -t or -it (sometimes with inte or redan in between).

data.name: The future: ska and kommer att
data.explain: Swedish often just uses the present tense for the future. Ska shows a plan or an intention: Jag ska resa. Kommer att says what will happen anyway: Det kommer att regna.
data.howToSpot: Look for ska or kommer att before a verb in its basic form.

data.howToSpot: Look for kan, vill, måste or får followed by a verb in its basic form (often ending in -a).

data.name: Adjectives match the noun: stor, stort, stora
data.explain: An adjective changes to match its noun. With en-words it has no ending (en stor bil), with ett-words it adds -t (ett stort hus), and in the plural it adds -a (stora bilar). This also happens after är: huset är stort.
data.howToSpot: Look for adjectives before a noun or after är, and check for the ending -t or -a.

data.name: The big car: den stora bilen
data.explain: When an adjective comes before a noun in the definite form, Swedish marks "the" twice: den, det or de comes first, the adjective ends in -a, and the noun has its ending too: den stora bilen, det stora huset, de stora bilarna.

data.name: Comparing: större, störst and mer, mest
data.explain: Most adjectives add -are and -ast to compare: billig, billigare, billigast. Some change more (stor, större, störst; bra, bättre, bäst), and many long words use mer and mest: mer spännande. "Than" is än.
data.howToSpot: Look for adjectives ending in -are, -ast, -re or -st, or mer/mest before an adjective, often with än.

data.name: Reflexive verbs: tvätta sig, känna sig
data.explain: Some verbs take a pronoun that points back to the subject: jag tvättar mig, du tvättar dig, hon tvättar sig, vi tvättar oss. Sig is for han, hon, den, det and de. Often English has no "self": känna sig means "feel".

data.name: Subordinate clauses: att han inte kommer
data.explain: In a subordinate clause (after att, som, när, om, eftersom…) words like inte, aldrig and alltid come before the verb: Jag vet att han inte kommer. In a main clause they come after it: Han kommer inte.

lines.sv: Men han märker att folk ofta talar mycket snabbt.
lines.en: But he notices that people often speak very fast.

data.name: Starting with när or om: När jag kom hem, åt jag
data.explain: A whole subordinate clause can be the first part of a sentence. The main clause then starts with its verb, and the subject follows: När jag kom hem, åt jag middag. Om det regnar, stannar vi inne.
data.howToSpot: Look for a sentence that starts with när, om, eftersom or innan; after that clause the verb comes before the subject.

examples.sv: När jag kom hem, åt jag middag.
examples.en: When I got home, I had dinner.

examples.sv: Om det regnar i morgon, stannar vi hemma.
examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay at home.

examples.sv: Eftersom bussen var sen, kom hon för sent.
examples.en: Because the bus was late, she was late.

examples.sv: Innan du går, måste du stänga fönstret.
examples.en: Before you leave, you must close the window.

examples.sv: Om du vill, kan jag hjälpa dig.
examples.en: If you like, I can help you.

lines.sv: När vi vaknade på midsommarafton, regnade det.
lines.en: When we woke up on Midsummer Eve, it was raining.

lines.sv: Eftersom vi hade bjudit tjugo gäster, blev vi lite oroliga.
lines.en: Because we had invited twenty guests, we got a little worried.

lines.sv: När gästerna kom vid tolv, var himlen fortfarande grå.
lines.en: When the guests arrived at twelve, the sky was still grey.

lines.sv: Om det regnar hela dagen, får vi äta inne, sa min man.
lines.en: If it rains all day, we'll have to eat inside, my husband said.

lines.sv: Innan vi åt sill och potatis, dansade vi runt midsommarstången i regnet.
lines.en: Before we ate herring and potatoes, we danced round the maypole in the rain.

lines.sv: Alla blev blöta, men ingen klagade.
lines.en: Everyone got wet, but nobody complained.

lines.sv: När maten var slut, slutade det plötsligt att regna.
lines.en: When the food was finished, it suddenly stopped raining.

lines.sv: Vi hoppas på sol nästa år.
lines.en: We are hoping for sun next year.

data.name: som: who, which, that
data.explain: Som starts a clause that tells you more about a noun: Mannen som bor här är läkare. It is used for people and things alike. When som is the object of its clause, it can be left out: boken (som) jag läser.
data.howToSpot: Look for som right after a noun, starting a clause that describes that noun.

examples.sv: Mannen som bor här är läkare.
examples.en: The man who lives here is a doctor.

examples.sv: Jag har en vän som spelar i ett band.
examples.en: I have a friend who plays in a band.

examples.sv: Det är filmen som alla pratar om.
examples.en: It's the film that everyone is talking about.

examples.sv: Var är boken som låg på bordet?
examples.en: Where is the book that was on the table?

examples.sv: De köpte huset som vi tittade på.
examples.en: They bought the house that we looked at.

lines.sv: Jag bor i ett hus med tolv lägenheter.
lines.en: I live in a building with twelve flats.

lines.sv: Kvinnan som bor under mig är pensionerad lärare.
lines.en: The woman who lives below me is a retired teacher.

lines.sv: Hon har en hund som skäller varje morgon.
lines.en: She has a dog that barks every morning.

lines.sv: Familjen som bor bredvid har tre små barn.

lines.sv: Högst upp bor en man som spelar piano.

lines.sv: Jag tror att det är ett hus som man trivs i.
lines.en: I think it's a building people feel at home in.

data.name: Questions inside sentences: Jag undrar om hon kommer
data.explain: A question inside a sentence is a subordinate clause, so the subject comes before the verb. Yes/no questions start with om ("if, whether"): Jag undrar om hon kommer. Others keep their question word: Vet du var han bor?
data.howToSpot: After words like undra, veta, fråga or förstå, look for om or a question word, then the subject, then the verb.

examples.sv: Jag undrar om hon kommer i kväll.
examples.en: I wonder if she is coming tonight.

examples.sv: Vet du var stationen ligger?
examples.en: Do you know where the station is?

examples.sv: Han frågade när filmen börjar.
examples.en: He asked when the film starts.

examples.sv: Jag förstår inte varför du inte ringde.
examples.en: I don't understand why you didn't call.

examples.sv: Kan du säga hur mycket det kostar?
examples.en: Can you tell me how much it costs?

lines.sv: Det var Elins första dag på det nya jobbet.
lines.en: It was Elin's first day at the new job.

lines.sv: Hon visste inte var hon skulle sitta.
lines.en: She didn't know where she should sit.

lines.sv: Hon frågade en kollega om det fanns kaffe.
lines.en: She asked a colleague if there was any coffee.

lines.sv: Kollegan visade henne var köket låg.
lines.en: The colleague showed her where the kitchen was.

lines.sv: Senare undrade Elin vem som var hennes chef.

lines.en: The boss had baked a cake and asked if Elin liked chocolate.

data.name: The passive with -s: byggs, byggdes
data.explain: Adding -s to a verb makes it passive: Huset byggdes 1920 ("was built"). It is common in news, signs and instructions: Här talas svenska. If the doer is named, it comes after av.
data.howToSpot: Look for verbs ending in -s where something is done to the subject (not verbs like finns or hoppas).

examples.sv: Huset byggdes år 1920.
examples.en: The house was built in 1920.

examples.sv: Här talas svenska.
examples.en: Swedish is spoken here.

examples.sv: Brevet skickas i morgon.
examples.en: The letter will be sent tomorrow.

examples.sv: Boken har översatts till tio språk.
examples.en: The book has been translated into ten languages.

examples.sv: Dörren måste stängas.
examples.en: The door must be closed.

lines.sv: Stockholms tunnelbana öppnades år 1950.
lines.en: The Stockholm metro was opened in 1950.

lines.sv: Sedan dess har den byggts ut många gånger.
lines.en: Since then it has been extended many times.

lines.sv: I dag används den av mer än en miljon människor varje dag.
lines.en: Today it is used by more than a million people every day.

lines.sv: Många stationer har målats av konstnärer.

data.name: His own: sin, sitt, sina
data.explain: Sin, sitt and sina mean "his, her, its, their" when the owner is the subject of the same clause: Anna ringer sin mamma (her own mother). Hennes or hans means someone else's: Anna ringer hennes mamma (another woman's mother).
data.howToSpot: Look for sin, sitt or sina; the owner is always the subject of that clause.

examples.sv: Erik målar sitt hus.
examples.en: Erik is painting his house.

examples.sv: De besöker sina föräldrar varje jul.
examples.en: They visit their parents every Christmas.

examples.sv: Hon glömde sin väska på bussen.

examples.sv: Barnen städade sina rum.
examples.en: The children tidied their rooms.

lines.sv: Maja flyttar från sin lägenhet i Uppsala.

lines.sv: Hon har packat alla sina saker i lådor.

lines.sv: Hennes bror Olle hjälper till med sin bil.
lines.en: Her brother Olle helps out with his car.

lines.sv: Majas pappa bär hennes säng.

lines.sv: Olle glömmer sin jacka i den gamla lägenheten.

data.name: Particle verbs: tycka om, komma ihåg, ge upp
data.explain: Many verbs have a small stressed word, a particle, that changes the meaning: tycka om (like), komma ihåg (remember), hälsa på (visit), ge upp (give up). The particle follows the verb, after the subject if that comes after the verb, and it carries the stress.
data.howToSpot: Look for a verb followed by a short word like om, upp, ut, på, av, fram or ihåg that changes its meaning.

examples.sv: Jag tycker om att dansa.
examples.en: I like dancing.

examples.sv: Kom ihåg att ringa mamma!
examples.en: Remember to call Mum!

examples.sv: Vi ska hälsa på mormor i helgen.
examples.en: We are going to visit Grandma at the weekend.

examples.sv: Stäng av datorn nu.
examples.en: Turn off the computer now.

examples.en: She looks tired.

examples.sv: Han gav upp efter en timme.
examples.en: He gave up after an hour.

lines.sv: I söndags gick vi upp tidigt.
lines.en: Last Sunday we got up early.

lines.sv: Vi skulle hälsa på mina kusiner på landet.

lines.sv: Men vi kom inte iväg förrän klockan tio.
lines.en: But we didn't get away until ten o'clock.

data.name: Pluperfect: hade + supine (hade ätit)
data.explain: The pluperfect is hade plus the supine: Vi hade redan ätit när de kom. It shows that something happened before another event in the past, just like English "had eaten".
data.howToSpot: Look for hade followed by a supine (-at, -t, -it), sometimes with a word in between.

examples.sv: När vi kom fram hade tåget redan gått.
examples.en: When we got there, the train had already left.

examples.sv: Hon hade aldrig sett snö förut.
examples.en: She had never seen snow before.

examples.sv: Jag insåg att jag hade glömt nycklarna.
examples.en: I realised that I had forgotten the keys.

examples.sv: De hade bott i Kiruna i tio år innan de flyttade söderut.
examples.en: They had lived in Kiruna for ten years before they moved south.

examples.sv: Han var trött eftersom han inte hade sovit.
examples.en: He was tired because he hadn't slept.

lines.sv: När Karin kom hem från resan hade någon lagt ett brev på hennes bord.
lines.en: When Karin came home from her trip, someone had put a letter on her table.

lines.sv: Hon kände genast igen handstilen.
lines.en: She recognised the handwriting at once.

lines.sv: Det var från hennes gamla vän Lena, som hon inte hade träffat på tjugo år.
lines.en: It was from her old friend Lena, whom she hadn't seen for twenty years.

lines.sv: De hade gått i samma klass och hade varit oskiljaktiga hela gymnasiet.
lines.en: They had been in the same class and had been inseparable all through upper secondary school.

lines.sv: Men efter studenten hade Lena flyttat till Kanada, och kontakten hade långsamt dött ut.
lines.en: But after leaving school Lena had moved to Canada, and the contact had slowly died out.

lines.en: In the letter Lena wrote that she had recently moved back to Sweden.

lines.sv: Hon hade hittat Karins adress genom en gemensam bekant.

lines.sv: Karin satt länge med brevet i handen innan hon ringde.
lines.en: Karin sat for a long time with the letter in her hand before she called.

data.name: If it were so: skulle + infinitive
data.explain: For things that are unreal or unlikely, Swedish uses the past tense in the om-clause and skulle in the main clause: Om jag hade mer tid, skulle jag lära mig piano. About the past: Om jag hade vetat, skulle jag ha ringt.
data.howToSpot: Look for skulle + a verb, often with an om-clause in the past tense nearby.

examples.sv: Om jag hade mer tid, skulle jag lära mig spela piano.
examples.en: If I had more time, I would learn to play the piano.

examples.sv: Vad skulle du göra om du vann en miljon?
examples.en: What would you do if you won a million?

examples.sv: Jag skulle aldrig flytta härifrån.
examples.en: I would never move away from here.

examples.sv: Om hon hade vetat det, skulle hon ha ringt.
examples.en: If she had known, she would have called.

examples.sv: Det skulle vara skönt med lite sol.
examples.en: A bit of sun would be nice.

lines.sv: Om jag fick välja, skulle jag bo på landet.
lines.en: If I could choose, I would live in the country.

lines.sv: Jag skulle ha en liten gård med höns och några getter.
lines.en: I would have a small farm with hens and a few goats.

lines.sv: På morgnarna skulle jag dricka kaffe på trappan och lyssna på fåglarna.

lines.sv: Så en dag kanske jag tar steget.
lines.en: So one day I may take the plunge.

data.name: The passive with bli: blev stulen
data.explain: Besides the -s passive, Swedish forms a passive with bli plus a past participle: Cykeln blev stulen. It often stresses a change or a single event. The participle agrees with the subject: huset blev sålt, cyklarna blev stulna.
data.howToSpot: Look for bli, blir, blev or blivit followed by a past participle (-ad, -d, -t, -en, or plural -na/-a).

examples.sv: Min cykel blev stulen i natt.
examples.en: My bike was stolen last night.

examples.sv: Han blev påkörd av en bil.
examples.en: He was hit by a car.

examples.sv: Huset blev sålt för tre miljoner.
examples.en: The house was sold for three million.

examples.sv: Vi blev bjudna på middag.
examples.en: We were invited to dinner.

examples.sv: Hon har blivit vald till ordförande.
examples.en: She has been elected chair.

lines.sv: Konserten i parken blev inställd i sista minuten.
lines.en: The concert in the park was cancelled at the last minute.

lines.sv: Scenen hade blivit skadad av stormen under natten.

lines.sv: Förhoppningsvis blir den inte inställd igen.

data.name: Words in -ande and -ende: spännande, sovande
data.explain: The present participle ends in -ande, or -ende after a long vowel (gående, leende). It works mostly as an adjective (en spännande film), as a noun (ett leende) or after verbs of movement (hon kom springande). Swedish never uses it like English "I am reading".
data.howToSpot: Look for words ending in -ande or -ende.

examples.sv: Det var en spännande film.
examples.en: It was an exciting film.

examples.sv: Barnen kom springande.
examples.en: The children came running.

examples.sv: Hon svarade med ett leende.
examples.en: She answered with a smile.

examples.sv: Vi ses på det kommande mötet.
examples.en: See you at the coming meeting.

lines.en: The journey to Kiruna was long but exciting.

data.name: Putting one part in focus: Det var Lisa som ringde
data.explain: To stress one part of a sentence, Swedish puts it between det är or det var and som: Det var Lisa som ringde (Lisa, not someone else). It is also very common in questions: Vem är det som har ätit upp kakorna?
data.howToSpot: Look for det är or det var, then the part in focus, then som.

examples.sv: Det var Lisa som ringde.
examples.en: It was Lisa who called.

examples.sv: Det är inte pengarna som är problemet.
examples.en: It's not the money that's the problem.

examples.sv: Vem var det som vann matchen?

examples.sv: Det var först i maj som snön smälte.

lines.sv: Någon har ätit upp alla kakor! Vem var det som gjorde det?

data.name: Verbs that always end in -s: hoppas, minnas, träffas
data.explain: Some verbs end in -s without being passive. A few only exist with -s (hoppas, minnas, lyckas, finnas), and some add it to mean "each other": vi träffas ("we meet"), de kramades ("they hugged").
data.howToSpot: Look for verbs ending in -s where nobody is doing anything to the subject.

examples.sv: Jag hoppas att du mår bra.
examples.en: I hope you are well.

data.name: Conditions without om: Hade jag vetat det…
data.explain: In formal or written Swedish, om can be dropped and the verb put first instead: Hade jag vetat det, hade jag stannat ("Had I known…"). Other verbs work the same way: Skulle du få problem, ring oss.
data.howToSpot: Look for a clause that starts with a verb (hade, skulle, är, har, blir…) but is not a question, followed by a comma.

examples.sv: Hade jag vetat det, hade jag stannat hemma.
examples.en: Had I known, I would have stayed at home.

data.name: Nominal style: actions turned into nouns
data.explain: Formal Swedish often packs actions into nouns: minska becomes minskningen, genomföra becomes genomförandet. Official texts are full of this style; in everyday speech a verb usually sounds better.
data.howToSpot: Look for nouns ending in -ning, -ande, -ende or -else that stand for an action.

data.name: The object first: Den filmen har jag sett
data.explain: Almost any part of a Swedish sentence can come first, to link to what was just said or to stress it, and the verb still comes second: Den filmen har jag redan sett. A preposition then often stays at the end: Det tror jag inte på.
data.howToSpot: Look for a sentence that starts with an object (often den, det or det där), followed directly by the verb and then the subject.

data.name: Long phrases before the noun: den nyligen renoverade stationen
data.explain: Written Swedish can put a whole participle phrase in front of a noun, where English uses a clause after it: den av kommunen renoverade stationen ("the station renovated by the council"). It is compact but formal.
data.howToSpot: Look for den, det, de, en or ett followed by several words and a participle before the noun.

data.name: Old wish forms: vore, må, leve
data.explain: A few old subjunctive forms survive in formal and fixed language. Vore means "would be": Det vore bra om … Others live on in set phrases and toasts: Leve brudparet!, Gud bevare oss, Må bästa lag vinna.
data.howToSpot: Look for vore, må, leve or bevare used to express a wish or something unreal.

data.name: Dropping har and hade: som han skrivit
data.explain: In written Swedish, the helper verb har or hade is often left out in subordinate clauses, leaving just the supine: Hon sa att hon redan ätit ("had already eaten"). It is never left out in a main clause.
data.howToSpot: In a clause after att, som, när, eftersom or sedan, look for a supine (-at, -t, -it) with no har or hade before it.

examples.sv: Hon sa att hon redan ätit.
examples.en: She said she had already eaten.

data.name: No matter how: hur … än, vad … än
data.explain: To say "however, whatever, whoever", Swedish frames a clause with a question word and än: Hur mycket jag än försöker, lyckas jag inte. Vad du än gör, ring inte honom.
data.howToSpot: Look for hur, vad, vem, var, vart or när followed later in the same clause by än.
